name: Digital Forensics
description: Forensic analysis, attack reconstruction, provenance, and incident response.
narrative:
Digital forensics at USENIX Security began with a practical scalability problem: enterprise attacks unfold over months, and the system audit logs needed to reconstruct them grow enormous. The earliest listed work tackled this head-on. "Dependence-Preserving Data Compaction for Scalable Forensic Analysis" (2018) showed how to shrink audit logs without losing the causal dependencies investigators rely on, while "SAQL: A Stream-based Query System for Real-Time Abnormal System Behavior Detection" (2018) let analysts query streaming system events to catch multi-step attacks as they happened. Together they framed the area's two enduring concerns: storing provenance efficiently and reasoning over it usefully.

The early 2020s brought a methodological shift toward learning and toward new computing substrates. "ATLAS: A Sequence-based Learning Approach for Attack Investigation" (2021) reframed attack reconstruction as a sequence-learning problem, moving the field beyond hand-built causality rules, while storage and tracking work like "SEAL: Storage-efficient Causality Analysis on Enterprise Logs" (2021) and "CLARION: Sound and Clear Provenance Tracking for Microservice Deployments" (2021) extended provenance to compressed logs and containers. The field also chased attacks into modern architectures, with "ALASTOR: Reconstructing the Provenance of Serverless Intrusions" (2022) covering serverless platforms, and broadened its notion of forensics to machine-learning systems with "Poison Forensics: Traceback of Data Poisoning Attacks in Neural Networks" (2022).

By 2023 the dominant theme was provenance-graph machine learning, with systems like "PROGRAPHER: An Anomaly Detection System based on Provenance Graph Embedding" (2023) and "AIRTAG: Towards Automated Attack Investigation by Unsupervised Learning with Log Texts" (2023) pushing detection accuracy. This success quickly invited scrutiny: "Evading Provenance-Based ML Detectors with Adversarial System Actions" (2023) demonstrated these detectors could be fooled, and "Lessons Lost: Incident Response in the Age of Cyber Insurance and Breach Attorneys" (2023) reminded the community that forensics is also a human and organizational process, not just a graph algorithm.

The most recent work is consolidating and critically re-examining the provenance-IDS paradigm. "MAGIC: Detecting Advanced Persistent Threats via Masked Graph Representation Learning" (2024) and "ORTHRUS: Achieving High Quality of Attribution in Provenance-based Intrusion Detection Systems" (2025) advance detection quality and attribution, while "Sometimes Simpler is Better: A Comprehensive Analysis of State-of-the-Art Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection Systems" (2025) audits whether the field's complex models actually outperform simple baselines. At the same time the area keeps expanding its scope to new domains, as "Principled and Automated Approach for Investigating AR/VR Attacks" (2025) brings provenance and auditing to augmented and virtual reality systems.

milestones.title: Dependence-Preserving Data Compaction for Scalable Forensic Analysis
milestones.note: established log compaction that preserves causal dependencies, defining the scalability problem at the field's core

milestones.title: SAQL: A Stream-based Query System for Real-Time Abnormal System Behavior Detection
milestones.note: introduced real-time stream querying over system events for detecting multi-step attacks

milestones.title: ATLAS: A Sequence-based Learning Approach for Attack Investigation
milestones.note: reframed attack reconstruction as sequence learning, the field's pivot from hand-built rules to ML

milestones.title: Poison Forensics: Traceback of Data Poisoning Attacks in Neural Networks
milestones.note: extended forensic traceback from systems to machine-learning supply chains

milestones.title: PROGRAPHER: An Anomaly Detection System based on Provenance Graph Embedding
milestones.note: exemplified the provenance-graph-embedding wave that became the dominant detection paradigm

milestones.title: Evading Provenance-Based ML Detectors with Adversarial System Actions
milestones.note: showed provenance-based ML detectors are evadable, opening adversarial scrutiny of the paradigm

milestones.title: ORTHRUS: Achieving High Quality of Attribution in Provenance-based Intrusion Detection Systems
milestones.note: pushed provenance-based IDS toward high-quality attribution, marking the paradigm's maturation

milestones.title: Sometimes Simpler is Better: A Comprehensive Analysis of State-of-the-Art Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection Systems
milestones.note: critically audited whether complex PIDS models beat simple baselines, signaling field self-reflection
